attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The required source lower bound is a barely-superlinear lower bound for a sparse explicit NP carrier on valid lengths; proving it already encodes superpolynomial SAT lower bounds in the unpadded parameter.
steps: Assume toward contradiction that SAT has P/poly circuits of size m^c for some fixed c.
Build the H_g circuit at valid length N_m by checking the delimiter/padding pattern in O(N_m) gates and feeding the prefix x to the SAT_m circuit.
Since g(m)->infty, eventually c/g(m+1)<1+epsilon/2, so the transferred circuit has size at most N_m^{1+epsilon}.
This contradicts an infinitely-often valid-length lower bound C(H_g,N_m)>N_m^{1+epsilon}; therefore no fixed c exists for SAT.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge is valid but conditional. It relativizes as a padding/circuit-transfer argument and does not evade natural-proofs or algebrization barriers for establishing the source lower bound.

assumptions: Fan-in-2 Boolean circuit size is the source lower-bound model; constants are absorbed by eventually large valid lengths.
The source lower bound is length-promise/i.o.; an all-length lower bound is impossible because invalid lengths reject by O(N) circuits.
g is fixed as part of the language, not supplied as advice; this blocks the prior unbounded-k nonuniform leakage.
SAT in P/poly means there is one polynomial exponent c with circuits for every input length m.
definitions: source object: H_g={x#0^t : x in SAT, |x|=m, |x#0^t|=N_m=(m+1)^{g(m+1)}} with nonuniform circuits measured only on valid lengths N_m.
target object: SAT in P/poly as the complete-language proxy for NP subset P/poly; the target consequence is NP not subset P/poly, not a direct proof of P != NP.
controlled interface: contrapositive circuit transfer SAT_m circuit -> H_g length-N_m circuit using one SAT circuit plus an O(N_m) parser and padding checker.
target-preserving condition: the lower bound is valid on infinitely many valid lengths, g(m)->infty, length validity is decidable in poly(N_m), and no advice beyond the SAT_m circuit is introduced.

equations.label: valid_lengths
equations.valid_when: Valid when the delimiter format fixes m and g is computable within polynomial time in N_m.

equations.label: upper_transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies after assuming SAT has m^c-size circuits and the parser uses only linear-size circuitry.

equations.label: threshold_absorption
equations.latex: g(m+1)>c/(1+\epsilon/2)\ \Longrightarrow\ C_{H_g}(N_m)\le N_m^{1+\epsilon}\text{ for all large }m
equations.valid_when: Requires sufficiently large valid lengths so constants and the O(N_m) checker floor are absorbed.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma fails if g is bounded, if the lower bound is demanded on invalid lengths, or if the carrier lets circuits choose among small padding exponents.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route bridge: replaces the previous common-epsilon family over all fixed k by one growth-padded NP carrier with an exact threshold transfer.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let g be unbounded, nondecreasing, and poly(N)-time checkable on lengths. If the growth-padded SAT carrier H_g has C(H_g,N_m)>N_m^{1+epsilon} for infinitely many valid lengths N_m, then SAT is not in P/poly, hence NP is not subset P/poly.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if H_g cannot be kept in NP with a poly(N) valid-length test or if the source lower bound reduces to an already-equivalent SAT lower bound with no simplification.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after choosing a concrete g, proving H_g in NP formally, and identifying a non-natural or otherwise barrier-aware lower-bound method for its valid slices.
control_decision.reason: The route now has a precise bridge lemma and a concrete threshold, while the source lower-bound obligation is sharply isolated.

dependency_updates.description: Replaced slogan by a proved contrapositive transfer for one growth-padded SAT carrier with threshold N^{1+epsilon}.
Source model is nonuniform circuits on infinitely many valid lengths of H_g; all-length formulations are quarantined.
Unbounded g supplies the missing quantifier over every polynomial SAT exponent c without a nonuniform family over k.
The bridge itself relativizes and is not a barrier breakthrough; any proof of the source lower bound must avoid or fall outside natural/algebrizing proof templates.

falsifiers: falsifier: If g is bounded by k, the consequence collapses to ruling out only SAT circuits below exponent about k(1+epsilon).
falsifier: If the source claim is all-length rather than valid-length/i.o., invalid lengths have trivial rejecting circuits and kill the lower bound.
falsifier: If a bundled carrier includes small k slices, those slices dominate the threshold and reintroduce the finite-exponent obstruction.
falsifier: If length validity or prefix recovery needs super-polynomial time in N, H_g may leave NP and the target-preserving transfer is invalid.

N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for H_g into exclusion of every SAT exponent c. This is route-level progress, not P vs NP; the hard obligation is now the sparse valid-length lower bound.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate g(r)=ceil(log log(r+4)); prove the verifier and length test are poly(N), then analyze whether valid-slice lower bounds for H_g admit a proof-complexity or MCSP carrier formulation.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The argument only kills templates satisfying full AlgTP. It does not classify proofs using algebra solely inside unrelativized SAT syntax, machine-code diagonalization, or proof-system soundness arguments.
steps: Typed the proof object as AlgTP(T,K), not as vague arithmetization.
Instantiated the claimed algebrized transfer at an arbitrary oracle O and admissible extension \widetilde O.
Chose a Baker-Gill-Solovay oracle A with P^A=NP^A.
Used K^A in NP^A and the collapse P^A=NP^A to obtain K^A in P^A.
Used polynomial recoverability A<=_T^p \widetilde A to simulate the P^A decider inside P^{\widetilde A}.
Derived K^A in P^{\widetilde A}, contradicting the AlgTP conclusion K^A notin P^{\widetilde A}.
Concluded that fully algebrizing templates are invalid for this target, while partial algebraic methods require a separate escape certificate.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a barrier certificate for a route class, not a lower bound for SAT or any NP-complete language.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: algebrization transfer audit

assumptions: K^O is obtained by the standard relativization of the verifier for K, so K^O is in NP^O.
For every admissible \widetilde O, there is a polynomial-time oracle procedure recovering each Boolean oracle bit O(x) from \widetilde O.
There exists a Baker-Gill-Solovay oracle A such that P^A=NP^A.
The proposed proof template claims full algebrizing validity, not merely use of algebra inside the empty-oracle proof.
definitions: source object: an arithmetizing lower-bound proof template T whose oracle dependence is mediated by low-degree extension access \widetilde O and whose source claim is K in NP \ P.
target object: the uniform separation NP not subset P, witnessed by a named NP language K and polynomial-time target reductions preserving oracle relativization.

controlled interface: nondeterministic verifiers may query O, deterministic algorithms in the algebrized simulation may query \widetilde O, and original O-bits are polynomial-time recoverable from \widetilde O.
target-preserving condition: T is accepted as algebrizing only if its empty-oracle proof transfers to K^O notin P^{\widetilde O} for all oracles O and admissible extensions \widetilde O.
admissible extension: \widetilde O is a standard low-degree extension representation with polynomial query-length and time overhead.

equations.label: AlgTP
equations.latex: \operatorname{AlgTP}(T,K)\Rightarrow \forall O\,\forall \widetilde O\supseteq O:\ K^O\in NP^O\ \land\ K^O\notin P^{\widetilde O}
equations.valid_when: Valid when the proof template claims algebrization and the target-preserving condition quantifies over all oracles.

equations.label: BGS-collapse
equations.valid_when: Valid in the classical relativized regime used to test oracle-invariant separation proofs.

equations.label: recovery-overhead
equations.valid_when: Applies when the algebraic extension exposes original oracle bits with polynomial overhead.

equations.label: extension-containment
equations.latex: P^A=NP^A\ \land\ A\leq_T^{n^{O(1)}}\widetilde A\Rightarrow NP^A\subseteq P^{\widetilde A}
equations.valid_when: Requires the collapse oracle and polynomial recovery of A from the extension oracle.

equations.label: contradiction
equations.latex: K^A\in NP^A\subseteq P^{\widetilde A}\quad\bot\quad K^A\notin P^{\widetilde A}
equations.valid_when: Requires the algebrizing transfer claim and the collapse oracle instantiated together.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If T only uses algebra in an empty-oracle syntactic argument, or restricts to an oracle family excluding BGS collapse oracles, this lemma does not kill it; the route must then state the nonalgebrizing escape feature precisely.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Certifies a route-level failure: fully algebrizing lower-bound templates cannot be valid proofs of NP not subset P.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let T be a proof template for a uniform NP language K notin P. If T satisfies AlgTP(T,K), meaning the same derivation proves K^O notin P^{\widetilde O} for every oracle O and every admissible low-degree extension \widetilde O encoding O, then T is not a valid route to P != NP. A Baker-Gill-Solovay collapse oracle A has P^A=NP^A, and recoverability of A from \widetilde A gives K^A in P^{\widetilde A}, contradicting the algebrized conclusion.

assumptions: The method is not allowed to infer K^O notin P^{\widetilde O} for arbitrary O.
The feature S must be mathematical data, not a slogan such as nonstandard or global.
Polynomial-time reductions used to reach K must remain uniform and must not introduce advice or nonuniform leakage.
definitions: source object: a partially arithmetized lower-bound argument T with an asserted syntactic or semantic escape feature S.
target object: a uniform statement K in NP \ P or NP not subset P over the empty oracle.
controlled interface: algebraic computations may be used locally, but any step depending on unrelativized machine encodings, Cook-Levin syntax, or proof-system soundness must be typed as S.
target-preserving condition: after removing all oracle-uniform transfer steps, the remaining derivation must still imply the empty-oracle separation with polynomial overhead only.

equations.label: escape-form
equations.valid_when: Valid when the route explicitly separates local arithmetization from oracle-uniform transfer.

equations.label: empty-target
equations.valid_when: Applies only after the syntactic escape feature preserves uniform polynomial reductions.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any proposed S that cannot be formalized independently of arbitrary oracle extensions or that requires advice to preserve the target theorem.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Creates a repair obligation for algebraic lower-bound routes rather than dismissing all arithmetization.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A route that uses arithmetization but rejects AlgTP must supply a named nonalgebrizing feature S and prove that S preserves the empty-oracle target theorem without silently restoring oracle-uniform transfer. Otherwise the claimed escape feature is undefined and the route remains quarantined.

control_decision.pivot_test: If the next route cannot state how it violates AlgTP while preserving uniform reductions, backtrack or quarantine it.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only a candidate with a named nonalgebrizing operation S and a valid empty-oracle target-preserving derivation.
control_decision.reason: A concrete falsifier shows that any proof transferring to K^O notin P^{\widetilde O} for all O cannot establish NP not subset P.

dependency_updates.description: Cycle 2 already quarantined fully relativizing templates using a collapse oracle; this cycle reuses the same oracle after adding extension access.
The natural-proof threshold audit remains active for large constructive truth-table properties; this cycle does not weaken that falsifier.
Full AlgTP(T,K) is inconsistent with BGS collapse plus polynomial recovery from low-degree extensions.

falsifiers: falsifier: the BGS collapse oracle A with P^A=NP^A invalidates any fully algebrizing separation transfer.
falsifier: if \widetilde A does not permit polynomial-time recovery of A, the target model is not the standard algebrization model and the lemma is not valid.
falsifier: a method depending essentially on empty-oracle Cook-Levin tableau syntax lies outside AlgTP and must be audited under L3-nonalgebrizing-escape-obligation.
falsifier: any route that says arithmetization escapes barriers but cannot name S has an undefined escape feature.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 3 converts algebrization into a precise route obstruction: AlgTP(T,K) plus standard extension recoverability contradicts the BGS collapse oracle. Algebraic lower-bound methods remain viable only if they identify a nonalgebrizing feature such as unrelativized syntax, nonblack-box machine encoding, or proof-system soundness, and then prove target preservation without advice leakage. This is valid route-level progress, not evidence for P != NP itself.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit one concrete nonalgebrizing candidate: an unrelativized Cook-Levin/proof-complexity route. Source object: lower bounds for a named proof system encoding SAT tableaux. Target object: SAT notin P. Test whether the proof-system lower bound transfers to uniform algorithms without natural-proof largeness, relativizing oracle transfer, algebrizing transfer, or nonuniform leakage.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The previous bridge did not require rho-dense target lengths. A length-balanced reduction n_m=Theta(m) is insufficient if the selected no-witnesses z_m exist only on a sparse set of m.
steps: Start with selected no-instances z_m for the source language A and compute y_m=R(z_m).
By target preservation, y_m is a truth table of an n_m-bit Boolean function f_{n_m} with circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon n_m}.
Uniformity of z_m and R gives bit access to f_{n_m} in time 2^{O(n_m)}, so the extracted sparse family is E-explicit.
For an arbitrary large n, use rho-density to find a hit length k=n_m in [rho n,n]. Define B_n(u,v)=f_k(u), where |u|=k and |v|=n-k.
If B_n had a circuit of size at most 2^{epsilon rho n}, fixing v would give a circuit for f_k of size at most 2^{epsilon k}, contradiction up to constant slack.
Thus B in E has all-length hardness 2^{Omega(n)}, which is the valid input form for the IW derandomization theorem.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a route-level carrier-transfer lemma, not P != NP. The unproved obligations are construction of E-uniform co-side no-witnesses, preservation of the GapMCSP NO promise at N^epsilon, and uniform length-density.

assumptions: Boolean circuit size is the target lower-bound measure; uniform bit access to R(z_m) is obtained by recomputing the relevant output bit in 2^{O(n_m)} time.
The density selector n -> m(n) is computable in poly(n), or is otherwise uniformly recoverable inside the E machine.
The IW consequence is invoked only from all-sufficiently-large length hardness 2^{eta n}, not from infinitely-often hardness.
No nonuniform selector, promise-violating reduction, or average-case interpretation is used.
definitions: source object: an E-uniform no-witnessed family (A,z_m) with A in DTIME(2^{O(m)}), z_m notin A, and z_m computable in time 2^{O(m)}.
target object: GapMCSP_{epsilon,delta} on truth tables y of length N=2^n, where NO means CC(y)>N^epsilon and YES means CC(y)<=N^delta for fixed 0<delta<epsilon.

controlled interface: a uniform many-one map R that on inputs of length m outputs a target truth table of length N_m=2^{n_m} in time poly(N_m), with n_m=Theta(m) on the extracted subsequence and no advice.

target-preserving condition: for every selected m, z_m notin A implies R(z_m) is a NO instance of GapMCSP_{epsilon,delta}, and the hit lengths n_m are rho-dense: for every large n some hit k=n_m lies in [rho n,n].

equations.label: threshold_translation
equations.valid_when: Valid when the target MCSP instance is literally a truth table of length 2^n and epsilon is a fixed positive constant.

equations.label: carrier_no_side_lower_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after the co-side reduction preserves the MCSP NO promise and the output length is 2^{n_m}.

equations.label: padding_density_transfer
equations.latex: k\in[\rho n,n]\ \wedge\ CC(f_k)>2^{\epsilon k}\Rightarrow CC(B_n)>2^{\epsilon\rho n}
equations.valid_when: Requires the dense hit length k to be chosen uniformly and B_n to restrict to f_k by fixing n-k variables.

equations.label: iw_target_consequence
equations.valid_when: Valid when the standard worst-case Impagliazzo-Wigderson hardness hypothesis holds for all sufficiently large input lengths over Boolean circuits.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any purported carrier whose NO instances occur only on target lengths with unbounded multiplicative gaps, or whose density selector is nonuniform.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Repairs the extraction theorem by adding the missing density obligation; separates valid E lower-bound extraction from invalid derandomization overclaim.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Length-dense E-uniform co-side reductions to GapMCSP at threshold N^epsilon yield an all-length E circuit lower bound 2^{Omega(n)} and hence the standard IW derandomization consequence. Without length density the same interface yields only an i.o.-E lower bound, so the derandomization transfer is not valid.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if no plausible source model can supply E-uniform rho-dense no-witnesses preserving GapMCSP NO at N^epsilon.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a named source, such as a proof-complexity or meta-complexity object, supplies dense co-side witnesses with uniform reductions to GapMCSP_{epsilon,delta}.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a checkable bridge lemma and a new falsifier, but the source construction and density obligation remain open.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier must include high-complexity truth tables at threshold N^epsilon on a rho-dense set of target input lengths, not merely infinitely often.
Extraction is valid for E lower bounds under uniform bit access; IW transfer additionally requires length-density and a uniform density selector.
Explicitness now includes uniform construction of z_m, bit computation of R(z_m), and computable selection of dense hit lengths.

The lemma itself is relativizing-style bookkeeping and does not evade barriers. Any proof of the source co-side high-MCSP carrier must be non-natural or outside the Razborov-Rudich obstruction, since it certifies explicit high circuit complexity.

falsifiers: falsifier: the carrier outputs high-MCSP truth tables only on infinitely many but multiplicatively sparse target lengths, giving no all-length IW hardness.
falsifier: R is many-one hard only as a promise reduction and does not map the selected co-side inputs inside the valid NO promise.
falsifier: the selected no-witnesses z_m require advice or search, causing nonuniform leakage into the extracted E language.
falsifier: the MCSP threshold degrades to N^{o(1)}, collapsing the padding transfer below 2^{Omega(n)}.
falsifier: the consequence claimed is only nonuniform i.o. lower bound, while the target statement needs uniform all-length hardness.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 3 identifies the missing quantitative invariant: length-balanced co-side GapMCSP reductions give valid sparse E lower bounds, but IW derandomization needs rho-dense all-length hardness. The route is therefore not blocked at extraction once density is assumed; it is blocked at constructing uniform dense no-side carriers without nonuniform leakage.
